text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The government approved the basic principles of pension reform, which will grant individuals more rights in ensuring their income after retirement.
- An investigation has been started about the strange robbery of the Oru peat plant workers wages. The bankruptcy administrator, who was relieved of 730,000 kroons, claims the affair to be political.
- The director of the central prison registered in his name a car belonging to an organised crime boss after the latter's arrest in 1995.
- The government plans to achieve 4-5 percent economic growth and to limit inflation to 10-12 percent, according to the programme for 1997-1998 approved on Tuesday.

- The families of the dead crewmen of the ferry Estonia disaster have lost interest in the investigation commission report, claiming that the officials are interested in the ship rather than the people.
- The Social Ministry and the UNDP signed a 2 million kroon agreement yesterday on the development of a poverty relief programme.
- Estonians in Abkhazia do not expect material but rather moral support from Estonia.
- The state prosecuting office will decide either tomorrow or next week, whether to bring embezzlement charges against Interior Minister Robert Lepikson.
- The daily reviewed a report of the biggest shareowners among parliament members. The two leading ones are Reform Party MP Ignar Fjuk and Coalition Party leader Tiit Vaehi.
- Saku Brewery will publish its quarterly results today and will continue on the stock exchange.
- A free trade agreement with Ukraine has not helped Estonian exporters much due to Ukraine's complicated certificates procedure.
